donorLifecycleFinding.claim: The donor's runtime-enforcement surface is much narrower than its file count suggests: only 5 refusal paths are live in the shipped app, and the planned capability set points mostly at code that never runs.
evidence: LIVE refusal paths (5): desktop mutation gate (main-commander.ts:701), software-action manifest gate (software-runtime.ts:88), Guardian-token gate (4 call sites), EvolutionHostOperations.authorize DENY throw (host-operations.ts:149), promotion gate Root-Surface stop.

The entire electron/capability/* layer is unreachable from production: createCapabilityBroker / invokeThroughBroker / evaluate / gateAuthorizer / authorizeExecution have ZERO non-test callers, and electron/main.ts:1003 builds new ExecutionGate() with NO options so the authorizer hook never fires.

RUNTIME-POLICY: loadRuntimePolicy is module-private with zero callers, electron/commander/runtime-policy.ts exports nothing, and no JSON-Schema validator exists in the repository. The runtime-policy JSON is hashed by repro-snapshot.ts and listed by a report script; it is parsed by nothing.
authority-planes.ts escalation rejection has exactly one caller, scripts/runtime-intelligence-diff-guard.cjs:64 (a CI script).

The named refuseSelfElevation / refuseOwnerIdentityChange / refuseDirectMainPush / refuseOwnerCredentialAccess / refuseRepositoryAdministration / refuseStaleShaPromotion / refuseArbitraryShell / refuseWorkspaceEscape and acceptOwnerClaim have ZERO production callers.
The Root audit ledger is written on live paths but read only by RootAuthority.history(), whose callers are tests.

NO cryptographic verification exists: createVerify / verifySignature / publicKey / x509 / createHmac = 0 hits in electron/ and src/. The only signing is an outbound GitHub App JWT; the ledger's chain is unkeyed SHA-256.

Dead code inside otherwise-live files: assessWorkspaceChanges (protected-surface-guard.ts:208, not exported), autonomousCeiling and protectedPathFor (root-authority.ts:341,346), EvolutionExecutionProfile's three assert* methods, guardedGrant (permission-manifest.ts:43), writeRootPolicy.
Two verdict-precision defects: authorization.ts reuses reason 'unresolvable-resource' for an unresolvable SUBJECT, and execution-authorization.ts reuses it for an unmapped execution KIND.
liveDonorPaths: electron/root-authority/root-authority.ts + root-audit-ledger.ts + root-policy-loader.ts + root-policy.ts (constructed live at self-evolution-coordinator.ts:359)
donorLifecycleFinding.conclusion: MB-002's capability-fabric/DONOR.json named MB-012 as the owner of the deferred Codex-Boss permission/authorization resolution (capability-broker.ts, authorization.ts, permission-contract.ts). This assessment finds that deferral is correctly closed as NO_VALUE: that entire layer has zero production callers in the donor, the donor's runtime-policy file has no consumer at all, and the parts that ARE live already have migrated or live Utopia counterparts (including the computer side-effect permission gate, which MB-008 migrated from the same src/shared/permission.ts).
